scope: Shared cast-trigger spell capture only; no card definitions/admissions/generated linkage changes.
problem: The old classifier skipped ordinary noninstant/permanent casts before inspecting queued copy consumers. The false prior_spells arm also required instant/sorcery, so a correctly queued optional artifact-copy trigger had no owned spell event.
implementation: CopyCastSpell{prior_spells:false} captures the actual triggering spell for an actual fresh consumer program, including artifact, creature and Aura spells.
Reuse the existing owned CopyEvent/SpellView payload, exact stack ID/departure refresh, copy allocator, copied cast choices, target editing, copy recipes and entry-to-token pipeline.

Keep prior-spell-count and chosen-X instructions instant/sorcery-only; keep CopyPreparedCastSpell at its previous instant-or-prepared eligibility; delayed next-instant/source-power paths remain below the unchanged instant-only gate.
No consumer means no new CopyEvent Box or CopyState allocation. Existing unconditional SpellView clone is unchanged.

rules_source.title: Official Aetherdrift release notes, Mendicant Core section
rules_source.basis: Permanent spell copies become tokens through resolution rather than token creation, and preserve original cast choices including X and paid additional/alternative costs.

wire_contract.delta: Previously absent noninstant single-copy cast-trigger packets can now own an existing CopyEvent. The schema199 prior198 assurance guard rejects this semantic population recursively, without erasing it.
inherited_preserved: Prepared CopyPreparedCastSpell captures, including mixed false/prepared programs in either order. A prepared marker alone never admitted an old false-only consumer.
Uncaptured inherited programs and nonconsumer packets.
wire_contract.selected_program: Guard uses SpellView::program, matching production classification for selected modal programs; it does not inspect only an outer raw Modal opcode.

validation: No Cargo/linker executed by author; runtime and production checks are root-owned after two exact-hash nonauthor source reviews.
